verdict.rationale: Crossmint lets an agent act autonomously within user-signed limits. A delegated signer key bound to a spend cap, allowed counterparties and a time window transacts with "no user prompt per action" (supp-4), and order intents give agents bounded allowances until expiry (supp-2). Webhooks can signal wallet and order events (docs-17, docs-38). However, Crossmint only supplies the payment rails the agent uses: the developer must build the scheduler and agent loop, and agent checkouts are poll-driven with user steering (supp-7, docs-50). Missing for 10: a first-party automation, scheduling or recurring-job feature; any documented background-execution runtime; independent or hands-on corroboration of unattended operation.
